action.dont_click: Do not click any link or open any file
action.dont_share: Never share your OTP, PIN or CVV
action.remember_otp: No check is perfect. Even a genuine OTP must never be shared with anyone.
action.verify_official: Check with your bank using the number printed on your card or on its official website
advice.courier_customs: A courier or customs office does not ask you to pay a fee to a personal UPI or bank account to release a parcel. Do not pay. Check the parcel in the courier company's own app or website.
advice.digital_arrest: There is no such thing as a 'digital arrest'. Police, CBI or courts do not arrest anyone over a call or video call, and never ask for money to close a case. Stop talking, do not pay, and keep the number and any screenshots.
advice.fake_qr: Scanning a QR code is only for paying someone. You never scan a code or enter your PIN to receive money or a refund. If you paid after scanning, money has left your account: call 1930.
advice.genuine: No check is perfect. Never share your OTP or PIN.
advice.investment_job: Promises of guaranteed returns or easy money from an online job are a warning sign. Do not send more money to 'unlock' or withdraw earlier payments. Keep every payment record.
advice.kyc_bank: A bank never asks you to complete KYC through a call, a message link or WhatsApp. Do not click the link or call the number. KYC is done at your branch or in the bank's own app.
advice.loan_app: A lender that asks for a fee before paying out, or threatens you or messages your contacts, is not genuine. Do not pay more because of threats. Save screenshots first, then uninstall the app.
advice.lottery_prize: You cannot win a prize in a draw you never entered, and a real prize never needs a fee first. Do not pay anything and do not share your bank details.
advice.other: Whatever happened, do not send more money, do not share any more codes, and keep every message, number and payment record.
advice.otp: An OTP, PIN or CVV is the key to your money. Never read it out, not even to someone who sounds like the bank. If you shared one, call your bank now.
advice.payment_request: You never need to enter your PIN to receive money. A 'collect request', a refund link or a 'wrong payment, send it back' message is a trick. If you approved a payment, money has left your account: call 1930.
advice.phishing_link: If you opened a link or installed an app, turn off mobile data and Wi-Fi, do not enter any more details, and uninstall the app. Then change your banking passwords and PINs from a safe phone. If you typed card or bank details, call your bank now.
advice.scam: Do not tap the link. Do not tell anyone your OTP or PIN.
advice.suspicious: Before you do anything, ask your bank yourself on the number printed on your card.

qr.cam.app.1: Open Chrome, tap the three dots, then Settings, Site settings, Camera. Make sure Camera is set to ask first, not blocked.
qr.cam.app.2: Look for this site in the Blocked list. Tap it, then choose Allow, or remove its permission.
qr.cam.app.3: Then press and hold the Suraksha icon on your home screen, tap App info (the ⓘ), then Permissions, then Camera, and choose Allow while using the app.
qr.cam.ask: When your phone asks to use the camera, choose Allow.
qr.cam.now_ok: The camera is allowed now. Tap Scan.
qr.cam.recheck: I turned it on, try again
qr.cam.reinstall: Deleting and reinstalling the app does not change this, because Chrome remembers the choice for the website.
qr.cam.web.1: Tap the lock next to the web address.
qr.cam.web.2: Open Permissions and turn on Camera.
qr.cam.web.3: If it still fails, allow Camera for your browser in the phone's Settings, under Apps.
qr.cam.why: A website cannot switch the camera on again once it has been turned off. It only takes a moment in your phone's settings:
qr.camera_note: The camera is used only while you scan. Nothing is uploaded.
qr.err.camera: Camera permission is off for this app
qr.err.camera_busy: The camera is being used by another app. Close that app and scan again, or take a photo of the code below.
qr.err.camera_dismissed: The camera was not allowed. Tap Scan again and choose Allow when your phone asks, or take a photo of the code below.
qr.err.camera_failed: The camera could not be opened. Try again, or take a photo of the code below.
qr.err.camera_none: No camera was found on this device. Take or choose a photo of the code instead.
qr.err.camera_unsupported: This browser cannot open the camera inside the app. Take or choose a photo of the code instead.
qr.err.none: No QR code found. Try again in better light, hold the phone steady, or choose a clearer picture.

reason.asks_id_details: It asks for Aadhaar, PAN or bank details.
reason.asks_secret_code: It asks you to share or send a code, PIN or password. Real banks never do this.
reason.authority_claim: It claims to be from the police, CBI, customs, a bank or another authority.
reason.callback_number: It asks you to call or message an unknown number.
reason.easy_money: It promises easy or guaranteed money.
reason.has_link: It contains a link. Do not open links you did not expect.
reason.impersonated_brand_action: It uses a known brand name with a suspicious link.
reason.install_app: It asks you to install an app or a remote-access tool.
reason.kyc_demand: It demands a KYC, PAN or Aadhaar update.
reason.model_pattern: The wording looks like scam messages seen before.
reason.no_flags: No warning signs were found in the wording.
reason.ok.official_channel_wording: It points you to official channels.
reason.ok.tells_not_to_share: It warns you not to share the code.
reason.ok.transaction_notice: It looks like a normal transaction notice.
reason.payment_request: It asks you to pay or transfer money.
reason.prize_claim: It promises a prize, lottery or free gift.
reason.script.courier_customs: It follows the known fake courier / customs scam script.
reason.script.digital_arrest: It follows the known digital arrest / fake police scam script.
reason.script.electricity_disconnect: It follows the known fake electricity disconnection scam script.
reason.script.fake_kyc: It follows a known fake KYC / bank scam script.
reason.script.lottery_prize: It follows the known fake lottery / prize scam script.
reason.script.unauthorized_order: It follows the known fake order / unauthorized charge scam script.
reason.secrecy_or_isolation: It tells you to keep this secret or stay on the call.
reason.short_or_odd_link: The link is shortened or looks odd, so you cannot see where it leads.
reason.threat: It threatens blocking, arrest or legal action.
reason.upfront_fee: It asks for a fee before giving a loan, job or prize.
reason.urgency: It pushes you to act immediately.
reason.url.ip_host: The link uses a number address instead of a website name.
reason.url.lookalike_brand: The address imitates a well-known name but is not its official site.
reason.url.many_subdomains: The address has many parts, a common trick to look official.
reason.url.no_flags: No structural warning signs in the link. This does not prove it is safe.
reason.url.plain_http_sensitive: It asks for login or payment on a non-secure (http) page.
reason.url.punycode: The address uses look-alike letters from another alphabet.
reason.url.shortener: It is a shortened link, so the real address is hidden.
reason.url.suspicious_tld: The address ends in a type often used for scam sites.
reason.url.userinfo: Text before an @ sign hides the real website.
report.advice.title: About this kind of scam
report.ch.bank_then_1930.title: Call your bank first, then 1930
report.ch.bank_then_1930.why: You shared a code or detail, so the thief may try to use it. Call your bank and your card or UPI provider right now, using the number printed on your card or passbook. Then call 1930.
report.ch.chakshu.title: Report it on Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi)
report.ch.chakshu.why: Chakshu on the Sanchar Saathi portal is for reporting suspected fraud calls and messages. It is not for money that is already lost: for that, call 1930.
report.ch.cybercrime_portal.title: File on cybercrime.gov.in
report.ch.cybercrime_portal.why: cybercrime.gov.in is the national cybercrime reporting portal, for harassment, fake profiles and other cybercrime, and for filing after a financial fraud.
report.ch.helpline_1930.title: Call 1930 right now
report.ch.helpline_1930.why: The sooner you tell them, the better the chance of stopping the money.
report.ch.tips.title: Good: nothing has happened
report.ch.tips.why: Stay careful. Never share an OTP or PIN, and check any message before you click.

step.block_cards: Block cards and UPI, and change passwords and PINs
step.call_1930: Call 1930 and tell them what happened
step.call_bank: Call your bank and card or UPI provider (number on your card or passbook)
step.dont_delete: Do not delete the messages, call records or chats
step.open_chakshu: Report the number and message on Chakshu
step.open_cybercrime: Then file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in
step.pay_bank: Call your bank now, using the number printed on your passbook or card, and tell them about the transfer. Note the transaction ID, and change your net banking password and PIN.
step.pay_card: Call the number printed on your card and ask them to block it now. Tell them about the charge and ask them to stop or check it.
step.pay_other: Keep any receipt, voucher or gift-card code, wallet address, and the name of the app or shop you used. Tell 1930 exactly how the money was sent.
step.pay_upi: Change your UPI PIN now. Then call your bank, using the number printed on your card or passbook, tell them about the payment and ask them to stop or check it.
step.read_tips: Read the safety tips and keep your OTP and PIN private
step.watch_followup: Watch for follow-up fraud calls and do not answer unknown callers about this
